headline: Oilers’ Mattias Ekholm out at least one week with upper-body injury
take:
Daily Faceoff reports that Edmonton defenseman Mattias Ekholm will miss at least one week with an upper-body injury, after he appeared to hit his head on the ice and was helped off by his teammates.

The numbers say the Oilers lose a steady piece. Ekholm has played 21.77 minutes a game so far this season, and when he is on the ice at 5-on-5, EDM controls 54.37 percent of the expected goals (a measure of chance quality). The team does about 6 percentage points better in that stat with him out there than without him. His own scoring is modest, with 1 goal and 2 assists in 9 games, so his value sits in how he drives play, not in points. That matters for an Edmonton team that is 7-1-1 but whose 5-on-5 share is only an even 50 percent so far this season, with goalies that have been about 2.6 goals worse than expected. The cushion is thinner than the record suggests.

Going by how the coach has used his players, since Ekholm has not yet missed a game, Jake Walman (14:17 a night) is next in line for his minutes. Expect Walman to take a bigger share of the ice time while Ekholm is out.
